Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Dinesh Kumar Paliwal

On The 10 th Of July, 2024
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 23450 of 2024
 (Ravi Ahirwar
 Vs
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh)
 Appearance:
 (Shri Sunil K. Pandey - Advocate For The Applicant. )
 (Shri Manoj Kushwaha - Panel Lawyer For Respondent/ State.
 )
 Order

This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.145/2024, dated 03.4.2024 registered at Police Station-Chhapara, District- Seoni (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 304-B, 498A of IPC read with Section 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

Applicant is in detention since 04.04.2024.
2.
As per the prosecution story, on 29.5.2019 deceased Bharti's marriage was performed with the present applicant.
On 30.3.2024 she committed suicide by hanging herself.

In the course of investigation it is revealed that on the occasion of Holi and Rangpanchmi, her mother had asked the present applicant to permit the deceased to go with her in parental house at Malkheda PS Chhapara.
Later deceased committed suicide.
In their statement, the parents have stated that she was being harassed in connection with demand of dowry of one motorcycle and Rs.50,000/- cash.
FIR was registered.
After investigation charge sheet has been filed.
3 . Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
In 2 MCRC-23450-2024 her life time, she never made any complaint against the applicant about demand of dowry.
She committed suicide only because he had not permitted her to go to her parental house.
All allegations are false and after thought.
Therefore, it is prayed that applicant may be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed grant of bail to the applicant.

5. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case including the material on record, but without expressing anything on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case Ravi Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115843878/
1 in which further pre-trial detention of the applicant is not warranted.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Consequently, this bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6 . It is directed that applicant - Ravi Ahirwar be released on bail on h is furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7 .
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case o f bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE 3 MCRC-23450-2024 mrs. mishra Ravi Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115843878/
2
